# What EpiExposure does?

`Introduzir o usuário ao workflow básico: da exposição ao modelo.`

```{r}
summarise_effects()
# =========================================================
# SIMULACAO: 520 epidemias x 86 dias
# 1 severidade por epidemia (DLNM-style)
# =========================================================

set.seed(123)

# -----------------------------
# Dimensoes
# -----------------------------
n_epi  <- 520
n_days <- 86   # 0–85

# -----------------------------
# Estrutura base (long format)
# -----------------------------
sim_data <- expand.grid(
  epi_id = 1:n_epi,
  dpp    = 0:(n_days - 1)
)

sim_data <- sim_data[order(sim_data$epi_id, sim_data$dpp), ]

# -----------------------------
# Inicializar
# -----------------------------
sim_data$tmean <- NA
sim_data$rain  <- NA
sim_data$rh    <- NA

# vetor final de severidade (1 por epi)
y_epi <- numeric(n_epi)

# =========================================================
# LOOP POR EPIDEMIA
# =========================================================

for (i in 1:n_epi) {

  idx <- sim_data$epi_id == i
  t_seq <- 0:(n_days - 1)

  # -----------------------------
  # Clima
  # -----------------------------
  tmean <- 25 + 5*sin(2*pi*t_seq/85) + rnorm(n_days, 0, 1.5)
  rh    <- 70 + 10*sin(2*pi*t_seq/85 + 1) + rnorm(n_days, 0, 4)
  rain  <- rpois(n_days, lambda = 3)

  # -----------------------------
  # ESTRUTURA DE LAG (CHAVE)
  # -----------------------------

  # efeito temperatura: forte em lags 5–20
  w_temp <- dnorm(t_seq, mean = 12, sd = 6)

  temp_effect <- sum(
    dnorm(tmean, mean = 25, sd = 4) * w_temp
  )

  # efeito chuva: acumulado em lags 10–30
  w_rain <- dnorm(t_seq, mean = 20, sd = 8)

  rain_effect <- sum(rain * w_rain)

  # efeito umidade: mais difuso
  w_rh <- dnorm(t_seq, mean = 15, sd = 10)

  rh_effect <- sum((rh - 60)/40 * w_rh)

  # -----------------------------
  # COMBINACAO FINAL (linear predictor)
  # -----------------------------
  eta <- 
    0.8 * temp_effect +
    0.05 * rain_effect +
    0.3 * rh_effect

  # -----------------------------
  # Converter para proporção (logit)
  # -----------------------------
  y_val <- 1 / (1 + exp(-eta/10 + rnorm(1, 0, 0.3)))

  # limitar
  y_val <- max(min(y_val, 0.95), 0.001)

  # -----------------------------
  # salvar
  # -----------------------------
  sim_data$tmean[idx] <- tmean
  sim_data$rain[idx]  <- rain
  sim_data$rh[idx]    <- rh

  y_epi[i] <- y_val
}

# =========================================================
# JUNTAR SEVERIDADE (1 por epi)
# =========================================================

y_df <- data.frame(
  epi_id = 1:n_epi,
  y = y_epi
)

sim_data <- merge(sim_data, y_df, by = "epi_id")

# ordenar novamente
sim_data <- sim_data[order(sim_data$epi_id, sim_data$dpp), ]

# =========================================================
# RESULTADO
# =========================================================

head(sim_data)

# checagem
table(table(sim_data$epi_id))   # deve dar 86 por epi
length(unique(sim_data$epi_id)) # 520 epidemias
```

```{r}
sim_data

cb <- define_exposure(
  wx_long = sim_data,
  vars = c("tmean", "rh","rain"),
  lag_max = 85
)

# construir design matrix
dat <- build_design_matrix(
  wx_long = sim_data,
  cb_templates = cb,
  lag_max = 85
)

# preparar resposta
dat <- prepare_response(dat, y_var = "y", family = "beta")


# ajustar modelo
fit <- fit_epidlnm(
  dat = dat,
  model_engine = "glmmTMB",
  family = "beta",
  random_effect = "epi_id",
  epiexposure_spec = attr(cb, "spec")
)

str(attr(fit, "epiexposure_spec"))

summary(fit)
t = predict_surface(fit = fit, wx_long = sim_data, var = "tmean", lag_max = 85,
                    uncertainty = TRUE, output = "summary", n_samples = 10)

t

tt = summarise_effects(fit = fit, wx_long = sim_data,
                  scale = "daily", effect_measure = "percent", uncertainty = TRUE, n_samples = 10,
                  output = "summary")




tt %>% 
  #filter(var == "rain") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(lag,effect))+
  geom_smooth(se = F)+
  facet_wrap(~var)

all_draws |>
  dplyr::count(var, value, lag, scale) |>
  dplyr::count(n)

tt %>% 
  filter(var == "rain") %>% 
  #filter(lag == 85) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(effect))+
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, color = "white")


```


```{r, eval = FALSE}

library(EpiExposure)

# carregar dados
data("TargetSpot")


TargetSpot
sim_temp <- simulate_exposure(
  lag_max = 85,
  mode = "pattern",
  pattern = "alternating_lags",
  alternating_values = c(25, 50),
  background = list(dist = "fixed", value = 0)
)

sim_rain <- simulate_exposure(
  lag_max = 85,
  mode = "pattern",
  pattern = "block_lags",
  block_lags = c(10, 30),
  fixed_value = 10,
  background = list(dist = "fixed", value = 0)
)

sim_humidity <- simulate_exposure(
  lag_max = 85,
  mode = "profile",
  background = list(dist = "normal", mean = 70, sd = 5)
)

pred <- predict_outcome(
  fit = fit_obj,
  profiles = list(
    temp = sim_temp$profile,
    rain = sim_rain$profile,
    humidity = sim_humidity$profile
  )
)
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# definir exposição (DLNM structure)
cb <- define_exposure(
  wx_long = TargetSpot,
  vars = c("tmean", "vpd"),
  lag_max = 85
)
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}

# construir design matrix
dat <- build_design_matrix(
  wx_long = TargetSpot,
  cb_templates = cb,
  lag_max = 85
)

```

```{r, eval = FALSE}

# preparar resposta
dat <- prepare_response(dat, y_var = "severity", family = "beta")
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# ajustar modelo
fit <- fit_epidlnm(
  dat = dat,
  model_engine = "glmmTMB",
  family = "beta",
  random_effect = "epi_id",
  epiexposure_spec = attr(cb, "spec")
)
```

` DLNM não é só modelo — é estrutura epidemiológica`
`define_exposure() define como a exposição atua no tempo`
`fit_epidlnm() estimula a relação exposição–doença`

```{r, eval = FALSE}
hist(dat$y_model, main="Distribution of disease response", col="steelblue")
```
